visa_type: Baylor Foundation Eswatini managed the visa application process and obtained a one-year work visa
how_obtained:
Baylor emailed a list of documents that needed to be completed (health screening, passport, background
check, etc) and sent and they handled the rest.
before_or_after_arrival:
I was not allowed to enter the country until the visa was approved, which caused issues with our start date. The
application process in Eswatini took several months (May-Aug)
who_paid: I paid for the background check, and Baylor paid the application fees
challenge_details:
As mentioned, the visa process took an extremely long time; my cofellow and I both turned in our applications in
early May and did not get approved until mid-August. We were not allowed to enter Eswatini until the visa was
approved, so we both worked remotely from the US for about a week and a half due to PiAf's start date window.
Now that we have our visas, we don't have to do any type of renewals during the year because they are
year-long visas, which is great, but getting them in the first place was really difficult.
advice_for_future_fellows:
Turn in everything that is asked of you as early as possible. The government systems of approval are reallyyyy
slow, and there is nothing that can be done to speed them up. Be sure to get everything notarized correctly and
have everything in the right format--they are very particular about that. The background check that they are
looking for is fingerprint-based and can be done at most UPS stores--it is not the kind they can print out for $20
at your local police station (I turned in the wrong one the first time).

visa_type: Single Entry Tourist Visa (second extension) and I have applied for a Student Pass
how_obtained:
Before arrival I applied online through evisa, for extensions once in country online eFNS with someone connected to ILRI bringing my
passport to immigration for an updated stamp
before_or_after_arrival: Before arriving
who_paid: placeholder
challenge_details:
We are the first fellows to be at ILRI for the full 12 months. Previously, Tim was never on campus, and the duration of a tourist visa was
sufficient for Brenda and Elliot. Therefore, prior to arriving, we asked what the visa procedure was and was told to apply for a single-entry
tourist visa. Two weeks into work, we received an email from the CapDev team at ILRI asking about our arrival, despite meeting one of the
team members on our first day of work. They had no idea when we were arriving. The miscommunication between the ILRI's CKM team and
CapDev occurred because CapDev manages all the fellows and the onboarding procedure for fellows is different than normal staff members.
We were told after arriving that we should have applied for a business visa and that we needed a police clearance (which for the state of New
York requires in-person fingerprinting) after arriving. I also found out that at the airport, I was only given 1 month instead of 3 months on a
tourist visa. Luckily, I was able to receive a police clearance from Medford Police Station near my university by email, otherwise, CapDev was
going to request for me to return home and obtain one. We have submitted our student pass applications, but in the meantime, I have
extended my tourist visa for the second time despite being told that doing so is risky. We've had many meetings where the CapDev team has
blamed this on us and the conversations have felt a bit hostile/condescending, and this miscommunication has made the transition much
harder. It is my first time living in another country on my own, so I have now learned a lot from this experience that will help guide me in the
future but simple conversations or questions properly answered would have made this less painful and avoidable. On a less stressful but still
disappointing note, without a resident card, leaving the country to explore others and paying park fees have been pushed back to next year
to save on paying the re-entry and non-resident fees. We are fortunate with our stipend and because Kenya is a large country with many
options, so we have still been travelling within the country.
advice_for_future_fellows:
David now understands and I also plan on informing the next fellows of everything they have to do. Like how once arriving, we let Asa and
Biafra know that they should get a police clearance.
